canonical_name: Elkin improved lower-bound construction for three-term-progression-free sets
category: 组合数学 / 计数组合
canonical_statement: There are a positive universal real constant c and a positive integer N such that, for every integer n at least N, the maximum size of a three-term-progression-free subset of {1, ..., n} is at least c times (n / 2^(2 sqrt(2) sqrt(log_2 n))) times (log_2 n)^(1/4).
canonical_claim: Elkin's asymptotic lower bound on the extremal size of a three-term-progression-free subset of the one-based integer interval, with the exact base-two formula and Omega binders.
statement_blocker: The exact arXiv v1 statement, one-based extremal root, ordered Omega binders, base-two formula, real coercion, source progression predicate, interval transports, mutations, and boundary policy are worker-self-tested. Dependency-ordered master acceptance remains the statement-node gate. Full SODA/journal comparison, lawful durable source admission, correction and errata audit, source-to-obligation mapping, and independent review remain H1 source debt rather than ambiguity in the frozen arXiv-v1 claim.
domain_and_universes: A closed Prop in universe 0: c and the quantitative expression are Real; N and n are Nat; the source interval is Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1); addRothNumber supplies its Nat-valued extremum, explicitly coerced to Real.
quantifiers: there exists a universal c : Real
there exists a universal N : Nat
for every n : Nat with N <= n
conclusion: c * elkinScale n <= (addRothNumber (Finset.Ico 1 (n + 1)) : Real), using the exact Elkin base-two scale.
degenerate_case_status: The positive threshold excludes n = 0 and permits n = 1, 2, and other small values to remain below threshold, matching the literal Omega statement. N itself is included by N <= n. The totalized scale and one-based intervals at n = 0 and 1 are separately kernel-checked.
